label: PanLex 2024 exact same-meaning Hebrew-English lexical expression

shapes.shape: hyphen with a letter (or apostrophe) on both sides
shapes.means: joins the parts of one hyphenated word or name (pot-belly, Stratford-on-Avon, CD-ROM)

shapes.shape: hyphen with a letter or digit on both sides and a digit on at least one
shapes.means: part of an alphanumeric designation or number (BM-21, K-9, 1-800-Missing)

shapes.shape: hyphen as the last character of the field, after a letter
shapes.means: the English is a prefix; the hyphen marks the side it attaches on (re-, un-, Sino-)

shapes.shape: hyphen as the first character of the field, before a letter
shapes.means: the English is a suffix; the hyphen marks the side it attaches on (-less, -shaped)

shapes.shape: hyphen with a space on both sides
shapes.means: a dash inside one proper name, joining a country's name to the capital that distinguishes it (Congo - Brazzaville)

shapes.shape: apostrophe with a letter on both sides
shapes.means: part of the word's own spelling: an English possessive or contraction (one’s, o’clock, I’m), an elision in a borrowed name (L’Orfeo, hors d'oeuvre), or a transliterated consonant (Sha’aban, Shari'a, K’op’ala)

shapes.shape: apostrophe at the start of a word (field start, after a space or a hyphen), before a lowercase letter
shapes.means: stands for letters clipped from the front of a colloquial form (’scuse, ’rents, 'til, 'cause)

shapes.shape: apostrophe at the start of a word (field start, after a space or a hyphen), before a capital
shapes.means: a transliterated ayin opening an Arabic place name (’Asir, ’Ara, Shefa-’Amr)

shapes.shape: apostrophe after a letter and before a space, a slash or the field's end
shapes.means: stands for a dropped final letter (burlin’, tho’) or closes a plural possessive (the ladies’)
examples: שירותים | the ladies’ room/the mens’ room

shapes.shape: period between letters followed by com/org/net/edu/gov at the end of the token
shapes.means: the dot of a web domain that is itself the name (Amazon.com)

shapes.shape: period after a single letter that has no letter before it
shapes.means: closes a one-letter abbreviation or an initial (U.S.A., a.m., e.g., A.C. Milan, ж. — a Russian source's feminine label)

shapes.shape: period after two or more letters, not a domain
shapes.means: closes a shortened word (Sat., approx., Mrs., ad loc., Ltd.)

shapes.shape: comma at depth 0 in a field whose every comma piece is one word (no space inside), none a bare conjunction and the last not 'to'
shapes.means: separates one English rendering from the next: PanLex's source dictionary packed several one-word equivalents into one expression (dam, fence, barrier)
examples: מיכל | container, ferry, vessel, vat, trough, tub, manger

shapes.shape: comma at depth 0 whose last piece is exactly 'to'
shapes.means: the dictionary inversion of an infinitive: 'lay-down, to' is the one verb 'to lay-down', its particle written after the comma

shapes.shape: comma at depth 0 in a field where some multi-word piece contains the word 'and' or 'or'
shapes.means: the comma of an English serial list inside one fixed expression (hook, line and sinker is one idiom, not two readings)

shapes.shape: comma at depth 0 in a field where every piece starts with a capital, some piece has more than one word, and no piece contains 'and'/'or'
shapes.means: the comma of a proper name in 'place, region' form: New York, New York is one name

shapes.shape: comma at depth 0 in a lowercase field whose earlier pieces are one word each and whose last piece is longer, with no 'and'/'or'
shapes.means: a packed scope: the trailing word of the last piece belongs to the earlier ones too ('get, become late' is get late / become late); the scope is not written, so the field is one reading

shapes.shape: comma at parenthesis depth > 0
shapes.means: notation inside an aside (none occur in this provider; kept so a new one is classified, not guessed)

shapes.shape: apostrophe with a letter on both sides
shapes.means: part of the word's own spelling: an English possessive or contraction (one’s, o’clock, I’m), an elision in a borrowed name (L’Orfeo, hors d'oeuvre), or a transliterated consonant (Sha’aban, Shari'a, K’op’ala)

shapes.shape: apostrophe at the start of a word (field start, after a space or a hyphen), before a lowercase letter
shapes.means: stands for letters clipped from the front of a colloquial form (’scuse, ’rents, 'til, 'cause)

shapes.shape: apostrophe at the start of a word (field start, after a space or a hyphen), before a capital
shapes.means: a transliterated ayin opening an Arabic place name (’Asir, ’Ara, Shefa-’Amr)

shapes.shape: apostrophe after a letter and before a space, a slash or the field's end
shapes.means: stands for a dropped final letter (burlin’, tho’) or closes a plural possessive (the ladies’)

shapes.shape: two ASCII apostrophes standing together as a whole token between spaces
shapes.means: typewriter quotation or ditto marks carried from PanLex's source, enclosing nothing; they hold no English and divide nothing (labor '' '')

shapes.shape: slash at depth 0 with no space on either side, each side a single capitalized word
shapes.test: (x) => { if (x.d !== 0 || /\s/u.test(x.p || " ") || /\s/u.test(x.n || " ")) return false; const [a, b] = slashSides(x.t, x.i); return words(a).length === 1 && words(b).length === 1 && UP.test(a[0]) && UP.test(b[0]); }
shapes.means: separates two names of one place in two languages (Elche/Elx): either name is a rendering

shapes.shape: slash at depth 0 with no space on either side, each side a phrase opening with 'the '
shapes.test: (x) => { if (x.d !== 0 || /\s/u.test(x.p || " ") || /\s/u.test(x.n || " ")) return false; const [a, b] = slashSides(x.t, x.i); return /^the\s/u.test(a) && /^the\s/u.test(b); }
shapes.means: separates the women's and the men's label of one facility (the ladies’/the gents’): each side is a complete English expression for it
examples: שירותים | the ladies’ room/the mens’ room

shapes.shape: question mark directly after '!'
shapes.means: part of a work's title as published (What the Bleep Do We Know!?)
examples: בליפ | What the Bleep Do We Know!?

shapes.shape: colon between two digits
shapes.means: separates hours from minutes (12:00 a.m.)

shapes.shape: colon after a letter, followed by a space and a capital
shapes.means: separates a title from its subtitle inside one work's name (Perfect Dark: Second Front)

shapes.shape: '!' at the start of a word, before a letter
shapes.means: a letter: the alveolar click of a Khoisan language name's own spelling (!Xũ)

shapes.shape: '!' directly before '?' after a letter
shapes.means: part of a work's title as published (What the Bleep Do We Know!?)
examples: בליפ | What the Bleep Do We Know!?

shapes.shape: underscore between two letters
shapes.means: joins a word to the class that disambiguates it, as a sense tag (Pole_person: Pole the person)

shapes.shape: '(' after a space, holding only capital letters (two or more) up to its ')'
shapes.means: opens an aside giving the name's official abbreviation (Macedonia (FYROM)); one reading

shapes.shape: ')' closing a '(' that holds only capital letters
shapes.test: (x) => { const o = parenOpenFor(x.t, x.i); return o >= 0 && /^\p{Lu}{2,}$/u.test(x.t.slice(o + 1, x.i)); }
shapes.means: closes the abbreviation aside

shapes.shape: '#' at the start of a word, before a letter, in a field that also carries '|'
shapes.means: residue of wiki link markup: the anchor sign of the link target (#Barcelona |Barcelona)

shapes.shape: '|' before a letter in a field that opens a token with '#'
shapes.means: residue of wiki link markup: divides a link's target from its display text, both the same name; not two readings

regions: one: the route is the whole definition in every row, so no mark's meaning can depend on a region (head, rendering list, notes) — the provider has none
